title: Finite type algebra with finite spectrum is finite-dimensional
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $B$ be a commutative $k$-algebra of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. If $\operatorname{Spec} B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has finitely many prime ideals, then every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal, $B$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space, and $\operatorname{Spec} B$ is a finite discrete space. The zero ring is allowed.

source.place: Lemma 00KH (Noetherian dimension 0) together with Lemma 0ALW (finite type algebra with finitely many prime ideals)

proof.text: By [lem-pqf-finite-spectrum-maximal-primes], every prime ideal of $B$ is maximal.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-dim-zero-finite] to the finite-type $k$-algebra $B$ and the conclusion of step 1. It gives that $B$ is finite-dimensional as a $k$-vector space (including the zero ring).

The points of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ are prime ideals, and a point is closed exactly when its prime is maximal. Thus every point is closed by step 1. Since the space is finite by hypothesis, the complement of any singleton is a finite union of closed singletons and is closed; hence every singleton is open. Therefore $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is discrete. The zero ring has empty spectrum, so the same conclusion is vacuous there.
